abstract: Rationale. Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is increasingly affecting populations worldwide and becoming a leading cause of psychological disabilities. However, MDD patients do not respond to current medications, resulting in treatment resistance. This situation demands more basic research to identify targetable molecules and the specific brain circuits and cell types that underlie negative affective pathology. Ras homolog family member A (RhoA) mediates negative affective-like behaviors via dendritic atrophy of nucleus accumbens (NAc) D1 (dopamine receptor 1)-Spiny Projection Neurons (SPNs), making RhoA a promising target for new depression therapeutics. However, the sufficiency of RhoA elevation in NAc projection-specific D1-SPNs is yet to be investigated. Objectives. Whether RhoA overexpression selectively in NAc-to-ventral tegmental area (VTA) SPNs (NAc-VTA SPNs) is sufficient to induce negative affective-like behavior. Whether chronic stress (CS) induces RhoA mRNA expression in this specific projection. Methods. A retrograde (Rg) vector expressing Cre recombinase was infused into the VTA together with Cre-dependent vectors overexpressing either a control expressing only enhanced Yellow Fluorescent Protein (eYFP) or RhoA-eYFP in NAc-VTA neurons. Mice then underwent a battery of affective assays (social interaction, etc.) and a two-choice sucrose operant task assessing motivation. RNA in situ hybridization (RHA-ish) quantified RhoA mRNA in NAc-VTA D1-SPNs of chronically stressed versus unstressed (control) mice. Results. RhoA overexpression in NAc-VTA SPNs, which are primarily D1-SPNs, elicited negative affective-like phenotypes, including social avoidance, reduced open-arm exploration, decreased grooming, and increased latency to approach food. RhoA and control groups acquired a food operant task similarly. However, RhoA overexpression significantly reduced operant responding and breakpoint during progressive-ratio testing. RhoA overexpression in the NAc-VTA projection neurons also diminished persistent sucrose-seeking behavior. Chronic stress induced RhoA mRNA expression selectively in NAc-VTA neurons.
